lines.japanese: 「鷹志君、ごはんできたよ」
lines.english: “Takashi, breakfast is ready.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、京ちゃん」
lines.english: “Thank you, Miyako.”

lines.japanese: 今日も食卓には僕の八分目を少し上回る量の食事が用意されていた。
lines.english: Once again, she had set out a little more food than I could comfortably eat.

lines.japanese: 学校に行っていたときはせいぜいこの半分しか食べていなかった僕には、少し食べるのがきついくらいの量だ。
lines.english: Back when I attended school, I had eaten no more than half this much. Finishing it all would be something of a struggle.

lines.japanese: だけど今日も彼女は僕に微笑んでくれるから――
lines.english: But today, once again, she smiled for me—

lines.japanese: ――まだ朝の寒さが優しい今の季節。彼女は薄手のカーディガンを羽織ってテーブルの前に座った。
lines.english: —It was the season when the morning chill was still gentle. She sat down at the table in a light cardigan.

lines.japanese: テレビは賑やかすぎるから点けない。彼女が実家にいる時も使っていたラジオから、くぐもったフォークソングが流れている。
lines.english: We left the television off because it was too noisy. A muffled folk song played from the radio she had used even when she lived with her family.

lines.japanese: 僕が座ると彼女は温かいお茶を注いでくれた。
lines.english: When I sat down, she poured me a cup of hot tea.

lines.japanese: 「いっぱい食べてね」
lines.english: “Eat plenty.”

lines.japanese: 目の前にある彼女の茶碗には、親指と人差し指の先を繋いだ程度のごはんしか入っていない。
lines.english: The rice in the bowl before her would barely have filled the circle made by touching the tips of her thumb and forefinger together.

lines.japanese: それでも山科さんの朝の食事量にしては多い方なんだ。仕事に出る僕のために、彼女は毎朝食事を作って一緒に食べてくれる。
lines.english: Even so, it was a generous breakfast by Yamashina's standards. Every morning she cooked for me and ate beside me before I went to work.

lines.japanese: 僕は箸を手にとって、水っぽいごはんを口に運んだ。
lines.english: I picked up my chopsticks and carried a mouthful of watery rice to my lips.

lines.japanese: 「えと、なかなか料理が上達しなくてごめんね」
lines.english: “Um... I'm sorry my cooking still isn't getting much better.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、そんなことないよ。作れるおかずの数も増えたじゃない」
lines.english: “That's not true. You can make many more dishes than you used to.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、叔母さんとポッポちゃんが親切に教えてくれるから」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. Your aunt and little Poppo have been very kind about teaching me.”

lines.japanese: 「叔母さんの域までは時間がかかるだろうけど、小鳩よりは上手になれるといいね」
lines.english: “It may take a while to reach my aunt’s level, but I hope you can at least get better than Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 「ポッポちゃんだって上手だよ。はあ、もっと家庭科の授業、真面目に受けておけばよかった」
lines.english: “Poppo is a good cook too. I wish I'd paid more attention in home economics.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いいよいいよ。おれは京ちゃんの料理好きだな」
lines.english: “No, it's all right. I like your cooking, Miyako.”

lines.japanese: 時間が少し気になったけど、ゆっくりめに食べて、山科さんの料理を味わうことにした。
lines.english: The time concerned me a little, but I slowed down and made sure to savor Yamashina's food.

lines.japanese: 彼女が羽田家に来て、初めて作ってくれたときのことを思いだすと、上手になったと思う。
lines.english: When I remembered the first meal she had cooked after coming to live in the Haneda household, I could see how much she had improved.

lines.japanese: 「あ、それと今日の帰りはちょっと遅くなっちゃうかも」
lines.english: “Oh, and I may be a little late coming home today.”

lines.japanese: 「病院？」
lines.english: “The hospital?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。先生が安定してるって言ってくれたんだけど、ときどき様子はみないといけないからね」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. The doctor says I'm stable, but I still need to be checked now and then.”

lines.japanese: 「早く治るといいね」
lines.english: “I hope you get better soon.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは少し眉を寄せながら、でも優しく微笑んでくれた。彼女のこの優しさがあれば、長い月日がかかっても、必ず治ると信じている。
lines.english: Yamashina's brow tightened slightly, but her smile remained tender. With her kindness beside me, I believed I would recover, however many years it took.

lines.japanese: 「でも、いつも帰ってくる時間にはメールしてね」
lines.english: “But send me a message at the time you usually get home, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、もちろんだよ」
lines.english: “Mm-hm. Of course.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ、ありがとう」
lines.english: “Hee hee. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 会社に着いたときとお昼休み、それと仕事が終わったあと。彼女と暮らすようになってから、この三つのメールを欠かしたことはない。
lines.english: One message when I reached the office, one on my lunch break, and one when I finished work. Since we began living together, I had never failed to send all three.

lines.japanese: たまに忘れたりして、彼女から心配のメールがくるけど、そのあとすぐに送れば彼女は喜んでくれるんだ。
lines.english: Now and then I forgot and a worried message arrived from her, but if I answered right away, she was always happy again.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあそろそろ行ってくるよ」
lines.english: “Well, I should be going.”

lines.japanese: 朝食を全て平らげた僕は、食器を運んで玄関に向かった。彼女が小走りで追いかけてくる。
lines.english: Having cleared my plate, I carried the dishes away and headed for the entryway. She hurried after me.

lines.japanese: 「いってらっしゃい」
lines.english: “Have a good day.”

lines.japanese: 「いってきます」
lines.english: “I'm off.”

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「寂しいな」
lines.english: “I'll be lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「京ちゃん……」
lines.english: “Miyako...”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、ごめん。よくないよね、せっかく家に居る私のために、鷹志君がお仕事してくれてるのに」
lines.english: “No, I’m sorry. That isn’t fair, is it? You’re out working for me while I stay at home.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、おれだって寂しいんだから、気持ちは一緒なんだ」
lines.english: “It's all right. I'll be lonely too. We feel the same way.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、そう言ってもらえるだけで、今日も一日頑張れそう」
lines.english: “Thank you. Just hearing you say that makes me feel as if I can manage another day.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあ行ってくるね」
lines.english: “Th-then I really am off.”

lines.japanese: 自分で言っておいてなんだけど、少し照れくさくなってドアを開けた。
lines.english: I had said it myself, but now embarrassment caught up with me, and I opened the door.

lines.japanese: 「あ、待って」
lines.english: “Wait.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　どうしたの？」
lines.english: “Hm? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、えっと……」
lines.english: “Well, um...”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「その、言ってほしいなって」
lines.english: “I... want you to say it.”

lines.japanese: 「言ってほしい？」
lines.english: “Say what?”
“You know...”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは俯いて黙りこんでしまった。出がけはときどき彼女がこうしてねだってくることを思いだす。
lines.english: Yamashina lowered her head and fell silent. Then I remembered that, every so often, she asked this of me before I left.

lines.japanese: 「京ちゃん」
lines.english: “Miyako.”

lines.japanese: だけど僕はいまだに慣れることが出来ず、すんなり告げることが出来ないんだ。
lines.english: Yet I had never grown used to it. The words still would not come easily.

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「好きだよ」
lines.english: “I love you.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは耳まで真っ赤にして、僕よりもっと恥ずかしそうに肩をすぼめている。
lines.english: Yamashina turned crimson to the tips of her ears and drew in her shoulders, even more embarrassed than I was.

lines.japanese: だからこそ僕は、彼女の髪を撫でてあげることが出来た。守ってあげたい。心からそう思えるから。
lines.english: That was why I found I could reach out and stroke her hair. I wanted to protect her. I felt it with all my heart.

lines.japanese: 「え、えっと……」
「じゃあ今度こそ行って――」
lines.english: “Then this time I really am—”

lines.japanese: 「待って」
lines.english: “Wait.”

lines.japanese: 腕にひとが抱きついてくる感触。僕は彼女の大胆な行動に驚いた。
lines.english: I felt her cling to my arm. Her boldness startled me.

lines.japanese: 一瞬だけ周囲を目をやって誰もいないことを確認すると、彼女の唇が僕の頬に撫でるように触れる。
lines.english: After a quick glance around to make sure no one was there, she brushed my cheek with her lips, tender as a caress.

lines.japanese: 「鷹志君が好き」
lines.english: “I love you, Takashi.”

lines.japanese: 「京ちゃん……はは、嬉しいけど照れちゃうな」
lines.english: “Miyako... Ha ha. That makes me happy, but it is embarrassing.”

lines.japanese: 腕に感じる彼女の感触。いつまでも側にいてほしいと願う。
lines.english: I felt her against my arm and wished she could remain beside me forever.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、いってくるね」
lines.english: “Then I'm off.”

lines.japanese: 振りかえる僕の背中で、山科さんが見送ってくれる。
lines.english: As I turned away, Yamashina stood behind me and watched me go.

lines.japanese: いま僕は、確かに幸せだった。
lines.english: In that moment, I truly was happy.

lines.japanese: 「受けとめてくれてありがとう――いつまでも私の傍にいてね」
lines.english: “Thank you for accepting all of me. Stay beside me forever.”

lines.japanese: 「永遠に、一緒だからね」
lines.english: “We'll be together for all eternity.”
